description: Identifier of the payment event given by the payment provider.
Order paid or refunded (-> stg_orders.order_id). An order can have one capture and one refund.
Date the payment provider captured or refunded the money (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD).
Payment method chosen by the customer: card, paypal, bank_transfer or apple_pay.

Amount of the payment event in EUROS with 2 decimals (e.g. 54.50 = fifty-four euros fifty), VAT included. NOT CENTS: a batch in cents (5450) must be rejected at ingestion - this is the CM 2 incident. Expected range 0 < amount <= 2000.
ISO 4217 currency code of amount. Always EUR today.
Last 4 digits of the payment card, used by Customer Service to identify a payment. Payment card data (PCI DSS): never join it with name or email in a report.
captured = money received from the customer; refunded = money sent back to the customer (amount is positive in both cases).
Identifier of the product.
Stock keeping unit, the product reference used by the warehouse.
Name of the product shown on the website.
Product category, written with a capital first letter.
Current catalogue price of one unit, in EUROS with 2 decimals, VAT included (may differ from the price paid on an order).
Company that supplies the product.
True when the product can still be sold.
Identifier of the order line.
Order the line belongs to (-> stg_orders.order_id).
Product sold on this line (-> stg_products.product_id).
Number of units of the product on this line.
Price of one unit at the time of the order, in EUROS with 2 decimals, VAT included.
Technical identifier of the customer account. One person may have several accounts (see duplicates).
First name given at signup, trimmed and written with a capital first letter ('MARIE ' -> 'Marie').
Last name given at signup, trimmed and written with a capital first letter.
Login email, trimmed and lower-cased.
Phone number as typed by the customer (format not standardised, may be empty).
Date of birth (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD). French DD/MM/YYYY, US MM-DD-YYYY and YYYY/MM/DD inputs are converted. Some impossible values remain (1899, future years) - see the CTP 2 scorecard.
City of the customer's address.
Country of the customer as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (FR, BE, DE, ES). 17 raw spellings are mapped; empty when the raw value was empty.
Date the account was created (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD), converted from 4 mixed raw formats.
True when the customer accepted marketing emails (GDPR consent). Marketing campaigns may only target rows where this is true.
Loyalty programme level, lower case: bronze < silver < gold < platinum ('Platinium' typo fixed).
Identifier of the order, given by the order system. One row per order_id (first copy kept when duplicated).
Account that placed the order (-> stg_customers.customer_id). 14 orders point to an unknown customer.
Date the order was placed (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD). Empty when the raw value could not be read (11 rows); a few dates are in the future (bug in the order system).
Lifecycle status of the order: pending -> shipped -> delivered, or cancelled / returned. 'canceled' (US spelling) is mapped to 'cancelled'.
Sales channel where the order was placed: web, mobile_app or marketplace.
Delivery country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (FR, BE, DE, ES).
Amount paid by the customer for the order, in EUROS with 2 decimals, VAT included, shipping included, before refunds (= gross revenue). Not cents.

**Customer** — a person who has created an account on ShopFast, identified by one `customer_id`.

- **Rule:** one row of `dim_customers` = one account (exact duplicate rows removed). One person with two emails can still have two accounts; merging them is a Steward decision.
- **Example:** 1 241 raw rows − 8 exact duplicates = **1 233** customers.
- Owner: Sara Martin (Head of Sales) · Steward: Karim Benali · Status: **approved (2026-11-25)**
First name of the customer.
Last name of the customer.
Login email, trimmed and lower-cased.
Country of the customer, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (FR, BE, DE, ES); empty when unknown.
Loyalty programme level: bronze, silver, gold or platinum.
Date the account was created (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD).
True when the customer accepted marketing emails (GDPR consent). Campaigns may only target true.
Number of orders ever placed by the account, all statuses included (cancelled too).

**Active customer** — a customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.

- **Formula:** `count(distinct customer_id) from fct_orders where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date > today − 12 months and order_date <= today`
- **Example:** on 2026-11-25, **1 080** of 1 233 accounts are active. A customer whose only order on 2026-03-02 was cancelled is **not** active.
- **Sales 6-month view:** a separate term, **recently active customer** (same rule over 6 months: 775 accounts on 2026-11-25), used only by the Sales dashboard and campaigns.
- Owner: Sara Martin (Head of Sales), aligned with Paul Girard (Finance) · Steward: Karim Benali · Status: **approved (2026-11-25)**
Sum of net_revenue_eur of all the orders of the account, in EUROS excluding VAT. 0 when the account never ordered.

**Order** — one purchase placed by a customer on one channel (web, mobile app, marketplace), identified by one `order_id`, whatever its status.

- **Rule:** one row of `fct_orders` = one order (duplicate `order_id` removed, first copy kept). Cancelled orders stay orders but are excluded from net revenue and from active customers.
- **Example:** 5 200 orders, of which 434 cancelled → **4 766** orders count for revenue.
- Owner: Sara Martin (Head of Sales) · Steward: Karim Benali · Status: **approved (2026-11-25)**
Account that placed the order (-> dim_customers.customer_id).
Date the order was placed (DATE, YYYY-MM-DD).
Lifecycle status: pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled or returned. Cancelled orders are excluded from net revenue reporting and from active customers.
Sales channel: web, mobile_app or marketplace.
Delivery country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (FR, BE, DE, ES).

**Gross revenue (EUR)** — total amount paid by the customer for an order, VAT included, shipping included, before refunds.
Owner: Head of Sales · Steward: Karim Benali · Status: approved (2026-11-10)
Sum of the refunded payment events of the order, in EUROS with 2 decimals, VAT included. 0 when nothing was refunded.

**Net revenue (EUR)** — money ShopFast keeps from an order: what the customer paid, minus refunds, without VAT.

- **Formula:** `net_revenue_eur = round((gross_revenue_eur − refunded_eur) / 1.20, 2)` — shipping fees stay in; cancelled orders are excluded when net revenue is summed for a period.
- **Example:** €120.00 paid, no refund → (120 − 0) / 1.20 = **€100.00**. €120.00 paid, €60.00 refunded → **€50.00**.
- **Not to confuse with:** gross revenue (VAT included, before refunds), still used by Sales for commissions.
